Here’s what happened in a simple way:

William I was the first “Emperor” (like a big king) of a new country called the German Empire, made in 1871. He was chosen to be the leader because lots of smaller countries joined together, and Bismarck (a very smart man who helped them join) helped make this happen.

But William I didn’t do much of the big decisions himself. Most of the time, Bismarck told him what to do. William I just said “yes” or “no” to what Bismarck suggested.

So, William I was like the boss, but Bismarck did most of the work to make the new country strong.

That’s what William I did!
